items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It was an octet, it was led by an old timer, his name was Shin Matsumoto... Matsumoto-san would play this Illinois Jacquet solo... Matsumoto-san was the tenor saxophone player.

ctx.x: And there was a black trumpet player—I don‟t remember the name, I don‟t really think I knew the name—he was, every once and a while, he rehearsed [with] the group. It was an octet, it was led by an old timer, he‟s a tenor saxophone player, his name was Shin Matsumoto—um, Shintarō, Shintarō? [repeats, Shin is correct]—I don‟t quite remember his … first name, but last name was Matsumoto, he was an old timer. He was considered the “Coleman Hawkins of Japan” [laughs]. But it was playing … that was very, very…
So you had tenor saxophone, trumpet, uh….
